text: One thing that happened yesterday, we have resolution of the Brenden Schooler saga, at least for now. And a week had gone by. This is about helping the rookies. My point is this, Watson choosing to be there. It's kind of a test. The slow time, the downtime. There's all sorts of ways that you will know as a coaching staff whether or not the contenders to be the starting quarterback are all in. Are they doing everything that they need to do on their own by their own idea, their own initiative? It shows how badly they want it. And I know it's their downtime. I get it. CBA requires that they have that time off. I I I understand. But you want to be the starting quarterback. You're in competition with somebody else. How do I win that competition? How do I convince the Browns coaching staff, if I'm the Deshawn Watson or Shadur Sanders, to pick me? How do I best position myself? It's beyond the fact that, you know, he's there to work out and help himself get better. That stuff gets noticed and that becomes a factor when the competition starts because week in and week out, if you're the starting quarterback, you want to see the commitment, the Tuesday commitment, the off day commitment. Are you down at Barnes & Noble looking for books or are you in the building working contributing to the game plan? Are you working on your body out at some other facility like Patrick Mahomes does? We know that from the quarterback series that he was featured in. We also know about Barnes & Noble from that series. So, look, it doesn't have to be a cynical view, a tactical maneuver. Let's just see who shows up. But I think it's relevant. Tom Brady has said when he was playing, if you want to beat me, you got to be willing to give up your life because I am. Well, if you want to beat Shadur Sanders and you're Deshun Watson, what do you do? If you want to beat Deshawn Watson and you're Shadur Sanders, what do you do? And I know that they say all the right things about being teammates, but there's only one quarterback. You got to view it as a competition that you intend to win. And if you approach it that way and you make sacrifices during your downtime, it's easy to extrapolate what you're going to do on your day off, what you're going to do on your by week. Are you all in? It's relevant in Minnesota, too. Kyler Murray, whose career has been tarnished by that ridiculous homework clause that was put in his second contract and all the talk about playing video games and not working. You know, that competition looks closer than we thought it was going to be. What's Kyler going to do? What's JJ McCarthy going to do? So this dead period when you have a true quarterback competition, this dead period is necessarily a test of who really wants it. May not matter at the end of the day, but it it could be the difference if it's close when it's all said and done. Hi, it's Mike Florio. Thanks for watching PFT on YouTube.
